title: Walker Daniel, Danville’s namesake
summary: Virginia lawyer Walker Daniel laid out the town at Crow’s Station in 1783, was the District of Kentucky’s first attorney general and was killed in 1784; Danville was named for him in 1787.

items.text: Daniel bought land from John Crow in 1782, laid off a town at Crow's Station in 1783 and gave land for the district court; the 1787 Virginia act named the town Danville for him.
First attorney general of the District of Kentucky (1783); killed in August 1784 near Bullitt's Lick by a party of about seven warriors, per a Virginia newspaper report.

timeline.event: District attorney general; lays off town at Crow's Station
